14. Capstone: a verbal-autopsy wide table

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-07-verbal-autopsy.Rmd
book-07-verbal-autopsy.Rmd

What you will learn

Combine age at death, labelled answers, calendar periods and cause of death in one private table.

This chapter uses the 24-person synthetic questionnaire test fixture described in Getting started. You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture()
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

The site connection is ready. This chapter creates its temporary questionnaire fixture locally.

Begin with the clinical question

We want one row per person, including people with missing information. Each row will contain a pseudonymous person_id, completed age at death, education and fever answers, first-visit calendar periods and cause of death. The analyst sees only summaries of those columns.

“Latest answer” here means the latest nonmissing answer to each question across all available history. It is not automatically restricted to before death or to the first visit. Define those restrictions explicitly for your actual study.

Keep the question separate from its answer 

education <- omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("observation", concepts = 900001L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"))
class(education)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

This is the same education definition as chapter 5. Reusing it keeps one categorical column with vocabulary names.

fever <- omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("observation", concepts = 900002L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"))
class(fever)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

The second question gets its own column. This capstone uses vocabulary labels Yes and No; chapter 5 demonstrated a user-defined lower-case recode.

Compute completed age at death 

age_at_death <- omop_age_at("death")
class(age_at_death)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

The default unit is completed years, using the full birth date and death date. It is not simply death year minus birth year. With the default partial-date policy, an incomplete birth date produces missing age; missing death also produces missing age. No January 1 birthday is silently invented.

Select the first visit once 

first_visit <- omop_anchor(omop_event("visit_occurrence"), which = "first")
class(first_visit)
#> [1] "omop_anchor" "list"

All calendar presentations below refer to this same first visit. An anchor is a selection rule; it is not a patient date returned to your R session.

Present its month 

visit_month <- omop_date(first_visit, omop_date_spec(precision = "month"))
class(visit_month)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

The values will be ordered categories such as year-month. No manual date-string mutation or fixed 64-boundary cut vector is needed in 2.10.4.

Present its quarter and year 

visit_quarter <- omop_date(first_visit, omop_date_spec(precision = "quarter"))
visit_year <- omop_date(first_visit,
  omop_date_spec(precision = "year", representation = "number"))
class(visit_quarter)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

Quarter labels distinguish both year and quarter. The numeric year variant is included to match the released native colleague recipe exactly. Precision is chosen separately for each variable.

Add the coded cause 

cause <- omop_variable(event = omop_event("death"),
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", value = "cause_concept_id"))
class(cause)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

The vocabulary supplies the label. People without death records keep missing cause and age, while remaining in the all-person output.

Assemble the released native recipe

The following completes the exact variable set in the released follow-up tools/dates/va-native.R, which closed the earlier feasibility gaps. It also includes age at first visit, exact visit/death dates and separate visit date parts so you can distinguish those types. Every one of these values stays on the server.

death <- omop_anchor(omop_event("death"), which = "first")
va <- omop_recipe(variables = list(
  age_at_death = age_at_death, age_at_first_visit = omop_age_at("first_visit"),
  education = education, fever = fever,
  visit_date = omop_date(first_visit), visit_month = visit_month,
  visit_quarter = visit_quarter, visit_year = visit_year,
  visit_parts = omop_date_parts(first_visit, c("year", "month")),
  death_date = omop_date(death), cause_of_death = cause),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"),
  options = list(translate_concepts = TRUE))
class(va)
#> [1] "omop_recipe" "list"

For a smaller analysis table, select only the variables your question needs using columns in omop_output(). The full version here is the regression-tested colleague recipe, rather than the old feasibility workaround.

Explain and assign 

explanation <- recipe_explain(va, conns = conns)
stopifnot(explanation$selected == "v2")
explanation$selected
#> [1] "v2"
print(recipe_execute(va, out = c(people = "D_va"), conns = conns))
#> people 
#> "D_va"

A successful symbol mapping means the server assigned the private wide table. It does not mean that a local object named D_va now holds patient rows.

Inspect column names 

dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_va", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#>  [1] "person_id"          "age_at_death"       "age_at_first_visit" "education"         
#>  [5] "fever"              "visit_date"         "visit_month"        "visit_quarter"     
#>  [9] "visit_year"         "visit_parts_year"   "visit_parts_month"  "death_date"        
#> [13] "cause_of_death"

The column list includes person_id. Its server values are pseudonyms. We do not print them or use them as local merge keys.

Summarise completed age 

dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_va$age_at_death", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean 
#>   33   33   33   38   43   43   43   38

In the synthetic patterns, supported complete birth dates give completed ages 33 and 43. The other patterns have incomplete birth or no death, so their ages are missing. The displayed summary is the actual aggregate returned by dsBase.

Show education and fever 

ds.omop.table("D_va", "education", conns = conns)
#> D_va$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6

Each education category represents an answer, not a separate column.

ds.omop.table("D_va", "fever", conns = conns)
#> D_va$fever
#> Yes  No 
#>   6   6

Missing responses are excluded from these counts. “No” is an observed answer, not an imputation for missingness.

Show the calendar periods 

ds.omop.table("D_va", "visit_month", conns = conns)
#> D_va$visit_month
#> 2020-03 2020-06 2020-07 
#>       6       6       6

These month counts group people by their first visit.

ds.omop.table("D_va", "visit_quarter", conns = conns)
#> D_va$visit_quarter
#> 2020-Q1 2020-Q2 2020-Q3 
#>       6       6       6

Several months can belong to one quarter; the grouped counts reflect that.

Show the cause categories 

ds.omop.table("D_va", "cause_of_death", conns = conns)
#> D_va$cause_of_death
#> Myocardial infarction             Pneumonia 
#>                    12                     6

All shown category tables contain labels, never numeric concept IDs. The recipe produces person rows privately; the book deliberately shows aggregates rather than a row preview, even though the development fixture is synthetic.

Recap

The native 2.10.4 API now supports the whole capstone: pseudonymous roster, completed age, coded answers, calendar periods and cause of death.

Try it

Use the short released helper to rebuild exactly the same recipe and verify its native plan equals the one above.

Solution

source("tools/dates/va-native.R")
reference <- va_native_recipe()
stopifnot(recipe_explain(reference, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
identical(recipe_to_plan(va), recipe_to_plan(reference))
#> [1] TRUE
print(recipe_execute(reference, out = c(people = "D_va_reference"), conns = conns))
#>           people 
#> "D_va_reference"
ds.omop.table("D_va_reference", "cause_of_death", conns = conns)
#> D_va_reference$cause_of_death
#> Myocardial infarction             Pneumonia 
#>                    12                     6
